text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Amsterdam AEX-index chalks new record high at 779.57. (p1)
- Junior finance minister thinks capital gains on investment in stocks etc. should be taxed at a separate rate of 25 percent. (p1)
- Financial services group Fortis' subsidiary merchant bank MeesPierson is to concentrate on small and medium-sized businesses in the Benelux. (p1)
- Publisher De Telegraaf puts down damages claim with broadcaster Tros for losing printing order for radio-TV guide. (p3)
- Finance ministry sees no harm in double role played by one of its top civil servants in privatisation of state automation company Roccade. (p3)
- Philips Electronics is to sell its Dryreed Switches plant in Heerlen. (p3)
- Royal Dutch/Shell may possibly reduce its refining capacity and buy refined products instead. (p4)
- First quarter turnover of the retail industry rises 4.1 pct compared to the year-earlier period. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Speculators force up coffee price. (p2)
- Machine producer for the chips industry ASM International reports disappointing first quarter results. (p17)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Majority of the Dutch do not want liberal party leader Frits Bolkestein for PM after next year's elections. (p1)
- Bankrupt sports-only TV channel Sport 7 pays 22 million guilders to its 240 creditors. (p7)
- Travel agencies and agents are to make regulations to prevent conflicts about fuel surcharge on flights. (p25)
- Large number of managers of medium-sized companies not fit for their tasks, according to research. (p27)
TROUW
- Agricultural ministry prolongs ban on transport of pigs by three weeks. (p6)
- Share price of technical wholesaler Reesink rises slightly on news of restructuring. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM and cut-price airline EasyJet in new conflict. (p13)
